title: Check yourself: Normalising results, command hooks and the practice

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A support agent uses three vendor systems: one gives epoch seconds, one a numeric status code, one local date text. The model keeps comparing dates wrongly. Which fix fits best, given that the team does not own them?

options.text: A longer system prompt that teaches the model each vendor's date format by example
options.says: Ruled out because a conversion in the model's head can be wrong, and the page assigns that task to code: "is a prompt for a task with a right answer".

options.text: A PostToolUse hook that supplies one readable format as the replacement output
options.says: The hook converts once, in code, for any tool, before the model reads the result.

options.text: A PreToolUse hook that refuses any call whose answer is hard to read for the agent
options.says: Ruled out because the hook runs after the tool and cannot refuse it: "The hook runs after the tool."

options.text: A larger model for the support agent
options.says: Ruled out because a larger model still converts by reasoning, and the page names the reliable place: "A PostToolUse hook is the place to make them consistent, once, in code."

questions.stem: A team commits a git-push guard to the project's `.claude/settings.json`. Its batch service runs the SDK with `setting_sources=[]` and a callback hook for refunds. A push attempt from the service is not blocked. Why?

options.text: The callback hook overrides every command hook that the settings define
options.says: Ruled out because the two kinds run side by side: "next to its callbacks, in parallel and with the most restrictive answer applying".

options.text: Command hooks are meant for interactive sessions of Claude Code only
options.says: Ruled out because the SDK collects "shell command hooks from settings files when the corresponding `setting_sources` entry is enabled".

options.text: The guard's timeout is too short for a batch service, so the call proceeds
options.says: Ruled out because the timeout is a setting of the command and says nothing about whether the file is read: "with the timeout in seconds".

options.text: Nothing reads that checked-in file here, so its shell commands are skipped
options.says: With no setting sources the SDK collects only the callbacks.
